item.title: BioNTech
item.description: Mainz, Germany mRNA biotech cofounded by Uğur Şahin and Özlem Türeci for cancer immunotherapy; employer of Katalin Karikó from 2013; Pfizer partner that took nucleoside-modified mRNA into a COVID-19 vaccine with reported 95 percent efficacy in November 2020.

item.title: Drew Weissman
item.description: University of Pennsylvania immunologist and MD-PhD who partnered with Katalin Karikó on nucleoside-modified mRNA; former fellow in Tony Fauci’s NIH lab, dendritic-cell vaccine researcher, co-inventor on Penn’s modified-RNA patent, and collaborator whose lab BioNTech later funded.

item.title: Elon Musk (b. 1971)
item.description: South African–born engineer-entrepreneur who, after Zip2 and the X.com/PayPal years, founded SpaceX (2002), became Tesla Motors’ lead financier then CEO, and by the mid-2010s ran concurrent electric-car and private-rocket industrial projects in the United States.

item.title: Emmanuelle Charpentier
item.description: French microbiologist who mapped CRISPR-Cas9’s tracrRNA–crRNA–Cas9 mechanism, coauthored the June 2012 Science gene-editing paper with Jennifer Doudna, cofounded CRISPR Therapeutics, and shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry; Isaacson does not state her birth year.

item.title: Feng Zhang (b. 1981)
item.description: China-born, Iowa-raised Broad Institute gene editor who adapted CRISPR-Cas9 for mammalian cells in a 2012–13 race with Jennifer Doudna and George Church, secured early Broad patents, cofounded Editas and Sherlock Biosciences, and remained Doudna’s principal U.S. rival through COVID CRISPR diagnostics.

item.title: Jennifer Doudna (b. 1964)
item.description: American biochemist and structural biologist at UC Berkeley who co-developed CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing with Emmanuelle Charpentier, raced Feng Zhang into human cells and patents, helped found Caribou, Editas (briefly), Intellia, and Mammoth, confronted He Jiankui’s germline edits, led Berkeley’s March 2020 COVID mobilization, and shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

item.title: Katalin Karikó (b. 1955)
item.description: Hungarian American biochemist who spent decades synthesizing therapeutic mRNA as a soft-money outsider at the University of Pennsylvania, co-developed nucleoside-modified non-immunogenic mRNA with Drew Weissman, joined BioNTech as a vice president, and saw that platform underwrite the Pfizer/BioNTech (and Moderna) COVID-19 vaccines.

item.title: SpaceX (Space Exploration Technologies)
item.description: Private American rocket company founded by Elon Musk in June 2002; developer of Falcon 1, Falcon 9, and Dragon; first privately built launcher to reach orbit (September 2008) and first commercial craft to dock with the ISS (May 2012), per Ashlee Vance (2015).

item.title: Tesla Motors
item.description: Silicon Valley electric-vehicle company incorporated in 2003 by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning; financed and later CEO-led by Elon Musk; producer of the Roadster and Model S through the 2008 near-bankruptcy, DOE loan, NUMMI/Fremont factory, and 2010 IPO as reported by Ashlee Vance (2015).
